newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt mostly higher with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt mostly higher with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging markets debt rose in line with U.S. Treasuries Thursday, tiring of its recent focus on unfolding Brazil bribery allegations, market experts said.

"Right now, the market is more driven by (U.S.) Treasuries and by expectations about (U.S.) monetary policy," said Kurt Schmid, head of propietary trading at SBC Warburg. "Fundamental local news is, at this point, not necessarily dominant."

Brady bonds traded lower with U.S. Treasuries after reports on U.S. consumer prices and jobless claims, but most rebounded after the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's business outlook survey came in weaker than expected.
Brazil "C" bonds were unchanged at 76-1/8 bid, holding steady despite further reports of alleged corruption in newspaper Folha de Sao Paolo.
On Thursday, Folha said taped telephone converstations suggested a high-level Cabinet member traded a television concession as well as cash for a legislator's vote on the key reelection amendment.
"The Brazilian scandal had a significant market impact up to yesterday," a Brady trader said. "At this point, it seems the issue can be contained and it's business as usual."
Investors remain cautious but optimistic about the developing situation, he said.
While the bribery allegations had the potential to delay privatization or reform efforts, next week's U.S. monetary policy meeting remained a more immediate focus, analyst said.
Most other Latin American Bradys rose Thursday. Argentina FRBs were up 1/4 at 92-3/8, and Mexico Pars were up 1/8 at 74 bid.
Murmurs that Mexico may buy back some of its Brady debt with proceeds from the new sterling Eurobond persisted Thursday, but traders extended the rumors little credence.
"There's nothing concrete -- it's just been a rumor floating around for three or four days," a Brady trader said.

European Brady debt turned in a more-mixed performance. Bulgaria FLRBs were up 1/4 to 51 bid, Poland Discounts were unchanged at 98-3/8 and dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans were up 5/8 at 84-1/2 bid.
